added.claim: A file input left empty in a browser form arrives as a part with filename="" and an empty body. MultipartParser.params() keeps the empty quoted value, so p.get("filename") is "" (not null), the part is spooled as a file part, and FormData.firstFile/files treat it as a file because they test only filename() != null. req.file("avatar") therefore returns a zero-byte UploadFile with filename "" instead of null, so the documented guard in the multipart.md example (if file == null -> 400 Missing file) never fires for a browser form, and file.save(dest) writes an empty file. multer (the Express counterpart the doc maps to) drops such a part. The behaviour is neither documented nor pinned by a test (no test or doc mentions an empty filename).
added.evidence: NaruServe-api/src/main/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/internal/MultipartParser.java:96 (filename != null branch) and params() keeps v="" for filename=""; NaruServe-api/src/main/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/internal/FormData.java:91 and :103 (filename() != null); docs/api/multipart.md:21 (file == null guard in the example)
added.suggested_fix: Either treat an empty filename with an empty body as an absent file (skip the part, still count it in maxParts) so req.file returns null, or state in docs/api/multipart.md that a browser sends filename="" for an empty file input and that handlers must check file.filename().isEmpty() / file.size() == 0; add a test with filename="" in either case.

added.claim: HttpExchange.sendFile has two different check orders in the two shipped adapters and the SPI Javadoc fixes neither. TinyHttpdExchange.sendFile validates the range first (IllegalArgumentException) and then the abort/single-start rule, while ServletExchange.sendFile runs requireStartable() first and the range after. On an already started or aborted exchange with a bad range, Tiny throws IllegalArgumentException and Servlet throws IllegalStateException/IOException. The Tiny inline comment ('the abort check and single-start rule win over a failed open') also contradicts its own order for the range check. The core never calls sendFile (DefaultResponse.sendBody streams through commit), so no user path is affected today; the SPI contract test only covers the happy range.
added.suggested_fix: Pick one order (start/abort rule first, as the Servlet adapter and the Tiny comment say), apply it in TinyHttpdExchange.sendFile, state it in the HttpExchange.sendFile Javadoc and add a shared SPI contract case for a bad range on a started exchange.
